 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Fresh from Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, Bayern Munich return to action on Wednesday, October 28, when they host second-tier side Magdeburg in the second round of the DFB-Pokal.
 Bayern will be aiming to maintain their title defense at the Allianz Arena, but the away side are coming in with confidence, having defeated Karlsruher SC 6-1 in the 2. Bundesliga. The last time these teams met in the German Cup, Magdeburg eliminated Bayern on penalties in 2000.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bayern Munich vs. Magdeburg Lineups and Team News
 Bayern Munich predicted XI: Jonas Urbig; Sacha Boey, Tarek Buchmann, Hiroki Ito, Konrad Laimer; Bara Sapoko Ndiaye, Leonard Prescott; Lennart Karl, Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari; Harry Kane.
 Harry Kane celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match SV Elversberg v FC Bayern München on September 13, 2026.Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images
 Joshua Kimmich is on leave for a family bereavement, while Manuel Neuer and Jamal Musiala remain unavailable. Luis Diaz is injured, and Minjae Kim and Aleksandar Pavlovic may return. Vincent Kompany is expected to miss the game, and assistant coach Aaron Danks will be in charge of the team.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Magdeburg predicted XI: Reimann; Nadjombe, Muller, McNulty, Nollenberger; Hyrylainen, Chavez, Musel; Iyoha, Zukowski, Atik
 Lubambo Musonda is out with an Achilles injury, and Momo Kwarteng is unlikely to be in the squad.
 Bayern Munich vs. Magdeburg Start Time Around the World
 Kickoff is scheduled for 8:45 p.m. local time in Munich on Wednesday, October 28.
 United States (ET): 3:45 p.m.
 United States (PT): 12:45 p.m.
 United Kingdom: 7:45 p.m.
 Germany and France: 8:45 p.m.
 South Africa: 9:45 p.m.
 India: 1:15 a.m. Thursday, October 29.
 United Arab Emirates: 11:45 p.m.
 Brazil: 4:45 p.m.
 Japan: 4:45 a.m. Thursday, October 29.
 Australia (Sydney): 6:45 a.m. Thursday, October 29.
 How and Where to Watch Bayern Munich vs. Magdeburg
 Germany: ARD and Sky Sport; stream on ARD Mediathek, Sky Go and WOW.
 United States: OneFootball.
 India: FanCode.
 France: L'Équipe and beIN Sports.
 Brazil: ESPN4 and Disney+ Premium.
 Japan: U-NEXT and GAORA On Demand.
 Austria: ServusTV and Sky Sport.
 International: OneFootball and DFB Play, where available.
 Bayern's official website will also provide a live text commentary and free web radio coverage. Streaming rights and subscription requirements differ by territory, so be sure to check your local listings before kickoff.
